title: Episode 258: 🇳🇴 An Algorithm Taxonomy (Serial, Parallel, Cooperative)

sentences.en: There are three types of algorithMs. There are serial algorithms, and there are parallel algorithMs. The third category, the third thing, is a cooperative algorithm.
sentences.zh: 算法分为三类。分别是串行算法、并行算法。第三类，也就是第三种，是协作算法。

sentences.en: I guess I was in the nascency of my parallel thinking, because before I joined NVIDIA, I was a serial thinker.
sentences.zh: 我想我当时还处于并行思维的萌芽期，因为在加入 NVIDIA 之前，我是一个串行思维者。

sentences.en: I only knew about category one, and then I joined NVIDIA, and it probably took me a year or two, really, to convert to parallel algorithm thinking.
sentences.zh: 我只了解第一类，后来我加入了 NVIDIA，大概花了一两年时间，才真正转变为并行算法思维。

sentences.en: But I still have not developed
sentences.zh: 但我至今还没培养出

sentences.en: cooperative algorithm thinking.
sentences.zh: 协作算法思维。

sentences.en: The beautiful thing about the parallel algorithms level is the seemingly sequential nature.
sentences.zh: 并行算法层面的美妙之处在于其看似顺序的本质。

sentences.en: The seemingly sequential nature is key.
sentences.zh: 这种看似顺序的本质是关键。

sentences.en: When I do reach for cub, I reach for device algorithMs.
sentences.zh: 当我使用 CUB 时，我用的是设备算法。

sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast, episode 258, recorded on September 23rd, 2025.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听 ADSP 播客第 258 期，录制于 2025 年 9 月 23 日。

sentences.en: My name is
sentences.zh: 我是

sentences.en: Connor, and today with my co-host, Bryce, we record live from Norway, right before NDC Tech
sentences.zh: Connor，今天我和我的联合主持人 Bryce 在挪威进行现场录制，就在 NDC Tech

sentences.en: Town.
sentences.zh: Town 大会之前。

sentences.en: In this conversation, Bryce explains his taxonomy of algorithms, parallel, serial, and cooperative.
sentences.zh: 在这次对话中，Bryce 解释了他的算法分类法：并行、串行和协作。

sentences.en: What's your mental model for the taxonomy of algorithms?
sentences.zh: 你对算法分类的思维模型是什么？

sentences.en: Because I guarantee you, as soon as you went, because Thrust, I feel like our listeners can relate to, even if they've never
sentences.zh: 因为我敢保证，当你开始接触 Thrust 时——我觉得我们的听众即使从未

sentences.en: touched Thrust, because a lot of our listeners are C++ people.
sentences.zh: 接触过 Thrust 也能产生共鸣，因为我们的听众很多都是 C++ 开发者。

sentences.en: And even if they're not C++ people, they're Rust people, they're Python people.
sentences.zh: 即使他们不是 C++ 开发者，他们也可能是 Rust 开发者或 Python 开发者。

sentences.en: They know the equivalence of a rotate, a copy, or whatever.
sentences.zh: 他们都知道 rotate、copy 或类似操作的等价物。

sentences.en: But then as soon as you drop down into block-aware algorithMs. So what's the taxonomy?
sentences.zh: 但一旦你深入到块感知（block-aware）算法层面。那么分类法是什么？

sentences.en: And we got to start there because you lost me and probably some of our listeners.
sentences.zh: 我们必须从这里开始，因为你刚才把我绕晕了，可能也把一些听众绕晕了。

sentences.en: Bryce looks excited, folks.
sentences.zh: 伙计们，Bryce 看起来很兴奋。

sentences.en: There are three types of algorithMs. There are serial algorithms in which you, a single thread
sentences.zh: 算法有三种。一种是串行算法，即你，一个单线程

sentences.en: calls the algorithm, and a single thread performs the algorithm, and the result is returned to a single thread.
sentences.zh: 调用该算法，由单个线程执行该算法，并将结果返回给单个线程。

sentences.en: That's what we're all familiar with.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们都熟悉的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Then there are parallel algorithms in which, let's start with cooperative algorithMs. No, we'll start with parallel algorithMs. We'll make more sense to people here.
sentences.zh: 然后是并行算法，其中……让我们从协作算法开始。不，我们先从并行算法开始。这对大家来说更容易理解。

sentences.en: Then there are parallel algorithms where you have the appearance of serial execution and a parallel algorithm in our nomenclature.
sentences.zh: 然后是并行算法，在我们的术语中，它表现为串行执行，但实际上是并行算法。

sentences.en: In like Thrust and in the C++ standard parallel algorithms, you have a single thread that, a single caller that invokes the algorithm.
sentences.zh: 比如在 Thrust 和 C++ 标准并行算法中，有一个单线程，即单个调用者来调用该算法。

sentences.en: And the algorithm then creates or acquires parallel execution resources and then runs the result, runs the computations on those parallel resources, that collection of threads.
sentences.zh: 然后该算法创建或获取并行执行资源，并在这些并行资源（即线程集合）上运行计算，得出结果。

sentences.en: And then that produces a result.
sentences.zh: 然后产生一个结果。

sentences.en: And then that result is returned to the caller.
sentences.zh: 最后将该结果返回给调用者。

sentences.en: In Thrust and in the C++ standard algorithms, it is returned asynchronously.
sentences.zh: 在 Thrust 和 C++ 标准算法中，它是异步返回的。

sentences.en: It's just the return value of the invocation.
sentences.zh: 它只是调用的返回值。

sentences.en: And so it's completely, seemingly sequential.
sentences.zh: 所以它看起来完全是顺序的。

sentences.en: But you could also imagine that this model also could apply to an asynchronous API, something that returns a future or a sender.
sentences.zh: 但你也可以想象，这种模型同样适用于异步 API，即返回 future 或 sender 的那种。

sentences.en: But the idea is that there's a single caller, a single thread initiates the operation.
sentences.zh: 但核心思想是，只有一个调用者，由单个线程发起操作。

sentences.en: The third category, the third thing is a cooperative algorithm.
sentences.zh: 第三类，也就是第三种，是协作算法。

sentences.en: In a cooperative algorithm, multiple threads decide to participate.
sentences.zh: 在协作算法中，多个线程决定共同参与。

sentences.en: So multiple threads call the primitive at the same time.
sentences.zh: 所以多个线程同时调用该原语。

sentences.en: And no execution resources are created or acquired by a cooperative algorithm.
sentences.zh: 协作算法不会创建或获取任何执行资源。

sentences.en: Instead, the calling threads that have called into this primitive,
sentences.zh: 相反，调用此原语的线程，

sentences.en: they donate their resources.
sentences.zh: 它们贡献出自己的资源。

sentences.en: So like examples of this is like, if people are familiar with MPI programming, like MPI collectives, like an MPI reduce or, you know, an MPI barrier, those are
sentences.zh: 举个例子，如果大家熟悉 MPI 编程，比如 MPI 集合通信（collectives），像 MPI reduce 或者 MPI barrier，这些就是

sentences.en: collective algorithms where all of the different ranks call it together.
sentences.zh: 协作算法，所有不同的秩（rank）共同调用它。

sentences.en: Or in, in, all of the different processes in a distributed computation, which are called ranks in the, in the distributed world.
sentences.zh: 或者在分布式计算中，所有不同的进程——在分布式世界中被称为秩——都在参与。

sentences.en: Or, you know, if you're doing like, like shared memory IPC, like you've got a, like, you know, you have a, uh, uh, uh, interprocess communication, like using shared memory to have
sentences.zh: 或者，如果你在做共享内存 IPC，比如你有进程间通信，利用共享内存让

sentences.en: multiple processes communicate.
sentences.zh: 多个进程进行通信。

sentences.en: And they're all invoking the same thing.
sentences.zh: 它们都在调用同一个东西。

sentences.en: They're all participating in some collective operation together.
sentences.zh: 它们都在共同参与某种集合操作。

sentences.en: That's a cooperative algorithm.
sentences.zh: 这就是协作算法。

sentences.en: In the case of CUDA, we, in CUDA, you launch these kernels, which are parallel functions that are executed by all the threads at once.
sentences.zh: 以 CUDA 为例，在 CUDA 中，你启动这些内核（kernel），它们是由所有线程同时执行的并行函数。

sentences.en: Within those kernels, you can invoke a cooperative algorithm, like a reduction, for example, where a bunch of threads all decide to participate in the reduction in each thread.
sentences.zh: 在这些内核中，你可以调用协作算法，例如归约（reduction），一群线程决定共同参与到每个线程的归约中。

sentences.en: Instead of having an input array, uh, what each thread, the inputs are distributed among the threads and each thread
sentences.zh: 而不是拥有一个输入数组，每个线程的输入分布在各个线程中，每个线程

sentences.en: contributes a value into the reduction, or maybe, maybe it's reduced some values locally, but each thread gives one piece of the input, uh, to the reduction.
sentences.zh: 向归约贡献一个值，或者也许是在本地归约了一些值，但每个线程都为归约贡献了输入的一部分。

sentences.en: Um, and all the threads have to contribute their piece of the input and then contribute to the, to the calculation.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所有的线程都必须贡献它们那部分的输入，然后参与到计算中。

sentences.en: And these cooperative algorithms are the building blocks that we use to implement the parallel algorithMs. And I was speaking in terms of
sentences.zh: 这些协作算法是我们实现并行算法的基石。我刚才是在

sentences.en: the, the cooperative level, but because, uh, that's how I often think about algorithms these days.
sentences.zh: 协作层面谈论的，因为这正是我现在思考算法的方式。

sentences.en: I, uh, suppose that's always been how I've thought about algorithMs. Um, I think that's how I default to thinking about it.
sentences.zh: 我想我一直都是这样思考算法的。嗯，我想这是我的默认思维方式。

sentences.en: You default to thinking about it at the, at the serial, serial or the parallel level.
sentences.zh: 你默认是在串行或并行层面思考的。

sentences.en: I, I, I've been, I always think about it at this level, but then when we converse, I often raise it up to the level that you're used to thinking about it.
sentences.zh: 我一直是在这个层面思考的，但当我们交谈时，我经常把它提升到你习惯思考的层面。

sentences.en: And you're usually thinking about it at a higher level of functional level and then lowering it down for me.
sentences.zh: 而你通常是在更高的功能层面思考，然后再为我降低到具体层面。

sentences.en: Well, so what I'll say folks, this is an inflection point in the podcaSt. When you, I mean, actually, I don't know when you started
sentences.zh: 好吧，我要告诉大家，这是本播客的一个转折点。当你……其实我不知道你是什么时候开始

sentences.en: listening, but back when we started this podcast in 2020, was it 20, was it 19?
sentences.zh: 收听的，但当我们 2020 年开始这个播客时，是 2020 年吗，还是 2019 年？

sentences.en: It was definitely, well, actually, I think we've said this before and then we looked it up and it was like, oh no, it was actually in the midst of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 肯定是……好吧，其实我们之前说过，后来查了一下，发现是在疫情期间。

sentences.en: But I thought you, we decided we were going to start it right after we went to Belfast and that was pre pandemic.
sentences.zh: 但我以为我们决定在去贝尔法斯特之后就开始，那是疫情前的事。

sentences.en: That was 2019, but we're about to find out folks, 252 episodes, 2020.
sentences.zh: 那是 2019 年，但我们马上就会知道，伙计们，252 期，2020 年。

sentences.en: I was wrong.
sentences.zh: 我错了。

sentences.en: I was, I knew I was wrong because we've done this before 2020 November, which was post pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我知道我错了，因为我们之前做过，2020 年 11 月，那是疫情之后。

sentences.en: I think we talked about it at Belfast, but then I didn't start it until a year later.
sentences.zh: 我想我们在贝尔法斯特讨论过，但我直到一年后才开始。

sentences.en: Anyways, when we started recording this, I was, I guess I was in the nascency of my parallel thinking because before I joined NVIDIA, I was a serial thinker.
sentences.zh: 总之，当我们开始录制时，我想我正处于并行思维的萌芽期，因为在加入 NVIDIA 之前，我是一个串行思维者。

sentences.en: I only knew about category one and then I joined NVIDIA and it probably took me a year or two really to
sentences.zh: 我只了解第一类，后来我加入了 NVIDIA，大概花了一两年时间才真正

sentences.en: convert to parallel algorithm thinking.
sentences.zh: 转变为并行算法思维。

sentences.en: But I still have not developed cooperative algorithm thinking
sentences.zh: 但我至今还没培养出协作算法思维，

sentences.en: because I primarily work in thruSt. And when I do work in cub, I feel like it's the, uh, Captain
sentences.zh: 因为我主要在 Thrust 中工作。当我使用 CUB 时，我觉得就像是……摩根船长，

sentences.en: Morgan, you know, when I do drink, I drink, whatever.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不喝酒，但如果喝的话，我就……随便吧。

sentences.en: He is the life of parties.
sentences.zh: 他是派对的灵魂人物。

sentences.en: He has never attended.
sentences.zh: 他从未参加过派对。

sentences.en: If he were to punch you in the face, he would have to fight off the strong urge to thank him.
sentences.zh: 如果他给你一拳，你还得努力克制住感谢他的冲动。

sentences.en: I have a week dedicated to him.
sentences.zh: 我有一周的时间是专门留给他的。

sentences.en: He is the most interesting man in the world.
sentences.zh: 他是世界上最有趣的人。

sentences.en: I don't always drink beer, but when I do, I prefer those sackies.
sentences.zh: 我不常喝啤酒，但如果喝的话，我更喜欢那些 Sackies。

sentences.en: Be thirsty, my friends.
sentences.zh: 保持渴望，我的朋友们。

sentences.en: When I do reach for cub, I reach for device algorithms, which is the equivalent of thruSt.
sentences.zh: 当我使用 CUB 时，我用的是设备算法，这相当于 Thrust。

sentences.en: The only algorithms I reach for are the device segmented reduce and device fixed segment reduce, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 我唯一使用的算法是设备分段归约（device segmented reduce）和设备固定分段归约等。

sentences.en: Uh, Bryce has something to add.
sentences.zh: Bryce 有话要补充。

sentences.en: When we started the podcast, I was at the place that you are currently at.
sentences.zh: 当我们开始这个播客时，我正处于你现在所处的阶段。

sentences.en: I was a few years into NVIDIA, but I was still thinking at the parallel algorithm level, not at the cooperative algorithm level, or maybe to some degree, I was starting to
sentences.zh: 我加入 NVIDIA 已经几年了，但我仍然是在并行算法层面思考，而不是在协作算法层面，或者也许在某种程度上，我开始

sentences.en: think at both, but having now five years later, I think about things first from the cooperative algorithm level.
sentences.zh: 两者兼顾了。但五年后的今天，我首先是从协作算法层面思考问题。

sentences.en: Um, and, and then from the parallel algorithm level.
sentences.zh: 嗯，然后再从并行算法层面思考。

sentences.en: And I think you are very close to jumping off the deep end because of the project that you're working on.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得你离彻底深入其中已经很近了，因为你正在做的那个项目。

sentences.en: I think, I think that a year or two from now, you're going to be where I am now because right now you are where I was a couple of years ago.
sentences.zh: 我想一两年后，你就会达到我现在的水平，因为你现在正处于我几年前的状态。

sentences.en: I can almost guarantee you that's true because the cub block primitives are what you use when you're writing kernels.
sentences.zh: 我几乎可以保证这是真的，因为当你编写内核时，你使用的就是 CUB 块原语。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I am about to start doing that folks.
sentences.zh: 伙计们，我马上就要开始做那个了。

sentences.en: We've only got segmented scans and reductions and we need more.
sentences.zh: 我们现在只有分段扫描和归约，我们需要更多。

sentences.en: And also we don't need the segments.
sentences.zh: 而且我们不需要分段。

sentences.en: We need fixed segments.
sentences.zh: 我们需要固定分段。

sentences.en: We need row wise and column wise, everything.
sentences.zh: 我们需要行向和列向，所有这些。

sentences.en: With the way we want people to program is at the parallel algorithm level.
sentences.zh: 我们希望人们以并行算法层面进行编程。

sentences.en: Um, because that is the level that's purest and closest to functional programming and array programming at the cooperative level.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为那是协作层面中最纯粹、最接近函数式编程和数组编程的层面。

sentences.en: You have to think about threads in synchronization at the cooperative level.
sentences.zh: 在协作层面，你必须考虑线程和同步。

sentences.en: You're programming threads.
sentences.zh: 你是在对线程进行编程。

sentences.en: And so it's always going to be an implementation detail for the work that we do.
sentences.zh: 所以对于我们所做的工作来说，它永远只是一个实现细节。

sentences.en: It's never going to be the programming model that we expose up to people.
sentences.zh: 它永远不会成为我们向用户展示的编程模型。

sentences.en: And so when you say what you just said, you think that I'm right, you, that, that you'll have to do that because you need X, you need Y and Z.
sentences.zh: 所以当你刚才那样说时，你认为我是对的，你必须那样做，因为你需要 X、Y 和 Z。

sentences.en: That's because you know that you need those things to be able to implement the backend of like, to be able to implement the algorithms that you want, not as a
sentences.zh: 那是因为你知道你需要这些东西来实现后端，比如实现你想要的算法，而不是作为

sentences.en: programming model that you'd expose to users.
sentences.zh: 一种向用户展示的编程模型。

sentences.en: So I think that in terms of this podcast, we will continue to primarily talk about things in terms of the parallel algorithms level, because the
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，就本播客而言，我们将继续主要从并行算法层面讨论问题，因为

sentences.en: beautiful thing about the parallel algorithms level is the seemingly sequential nature.
sentences.zh: 并行算法层面的美妙之处在于其看似顺序的本质。

sentences.en: The seemingly sequential nature is key.
sentences.zh: 这种看似顺序的本质是关键。

sentences.en: I mean, and this is, uh, Bryce just admitted something that he may or may not have wanted to admit is that he said, you know, we want people to program at the functional
sentences.zh: 我是说，Bryce 刚刚承认了一件他可能并不想承认的事，他说，你知道，我们希望人们在函数式

sentences.en: or array level.
sentences.zh: 或数组层面进行编程。

sentences.en: And so he said, he just said, of course, off, off mic.
sentences.zh: 所以他刚才在麦克风外说了。

sentences.en: And this is the point, you know, we are C plus plus, we are CUDA C plus plus, uh, programmers, developers, but the array
sentences.zh: 这就是重点，你知道，我们是 C++，我们是 CUDA C++ 程序员、开发者，但数组

sentences.en: programming model, the functional programming model, it's just easier to reason about everybody that's hating on all Haskell, OCaml, guess what?
sentences.zh: 编程模型、函数式编程模型，更容易理解。所有讨厌 Haskell、OCaml 的人，猜猜怎么着？

sentences.en: It's a better model.
sentences.zh: 这是一个更好的模型。

sentences.en: It's just not performant, but guess what we hear a promise to the listener is we're going to make the easy way be the efficient way.
sentences.zh: 它只是性能不够好，但猜猜我们对听众的承诺是什么？我们要让简单的方法成为高效的方法。

sentences.en: And that's the dream.
sentences.zh: 这就是梦想。

sentences.en: That's the dream.
sentences.zh: 这就是梦想。

sentences.en: And yes, there are trade-offs, but we're going to make it happen.
sentences.zh: 是的，会有权衡，但我们会实现它。

sentences.en: Bryce has got something to add.
sentences.zh: Bryce 有话要补充。

sentences.en: It's not always the case that it's less efficient to write the functional or the array or just the higher level code.
sentences.zh: 编写函数式、数组式或仅仅是更高级的代码，并不总是效率更低。

sentences.en: If you write the lower level code, you are baking in certain details and you're making certain assumptions about how the, about the, like the nature of what you're executing on.
sentences.zh: 如果你编写底层代码，你就是在固化某些细节，并对你执行的环境性质做出某些假设。

sentences.en: Like if you're programming to threads as you do in a cooperative model, then you're, you're making certain assumptions about quantities of threads and,
sentences.zh: 比如，如果你像在协作模型中那样针对线程进行编程，那么你就在对线程数量做出某些假设，以及

sentences.en: uh, how those threads are going to communicate with, with each other.
sentences.zh: 这些线程将如何相互通信。

sentences.en: Whereas if you, if you express things at the array slash functional level, you're expressing things purely in terms of like the
sentences.zh: 而如果你在数组/函数式层面表达事物，你纯粹是根据需求来表达，

sentences.en: requirements, you're not saying anything about how it needs to be implemented, right?
sentences.zh: 你没有说明它需要如何实现，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, like it's, um, it's, it's, it's just, it's descriptive versus prescriptive, right?
sentences.zh: 就像……它是描述性的，而不是规定性的，对吧？

sentences.en: Array and functional is descriptive.
sentences.zh: 数组和函数式是描述性的。

sentences.en: You're describing what it does.
sentences.zh: 你在描述它做什么。

sentences.en: Whereas cooperative is prescriptive.
sentences.zh: 而协作是规定性的。

sentences.en: You're saying it must be done this way.
sentences.zh: 你在说它必须以这种方式完成。

sentences.en: And I think the history of parallel programming has actually shown that descriptive models tend to win over prescriptive models.
sentences.zh: 我认为并行编程的历史实际上已经证明，描述性模型往往胜过规定性模型。

sentences.en: There it is folks, array functional.
sentences.zh: 就是这样，伙计们，数组函数式。
